AWAR D Preface 1.

Detailed Accident Reports (DAR) in case of death of - (i)
Tony; (ii) Tejas and bodily injury to (iii) Gaurav are taken up to be decided simultaneously.
Background 2.

As gleaned from Final Report in FIR No.234/2022 PS Jaffarpur Kalan - Gaurav, Tony and Tejas returning home riding motorcycle No.DL-8SBH-9754 after attending marriage function at Radhey Shyam Vatika, Surhera, Delhi met with an accident near Dharampal Piyao, Mundhela Khurd Village,
Delhi on 08.12.2022 at about 9:06 pm after their motorcycle was hit by White Colour Taxi No.
DL-1ZD-2211 coming from opposite side in rash and negligent manner.
They were shifted to RTRM Hospital, where Tony admitted upon MLC No.7304/22 was declared 'Brought Dead'.
His younger brother Tejas admitted upon MLC No.7302/22 was referred to Higher Centre but succumbed to injuries in course of treatment at Tarak Hospital, Dwarka Mor, Delhi.
3. FIR No.234/22 under section 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Jaffarpur Kalan on 09.12.2022 and site-plan was prepared by IO.

Respondent Pawan Kumar produced by ASI Ranvir Singh, In-charge, PCR Van along with MLC No.7305/22 was formally arrested and released on police bail and dead bodies of Tony and Tejas were handed over to their relatives after identification and postmortem examination.

Documents viz. DL, RC, Fitness and Policy produced by respondent were verified from concerned authorities and offence under section 185 M.V. Act was added on the basis of MLC No.7305/22 of Pawan Kumar recording Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) 127 mg/ml.

Statement of Gaurav (petitioner herein) was recorded who alleged that White Taxi coming from opposite side hit their motorcycle on the left side of road and offence under section 338 IPC was also added on the basis of final opinion of grievous injury upon his MLC.
IO, thereafter, concluded investigation and prepared DAR which was filed in Court along with copy of Final Report under section 279/338/304A IPC & 185 M.V. Act.

18. Though, witness has admitted that none of the victim was wearing any helmet or holding any licence at the time of accident, however, his testimony remained consistent and nothing material could be elicited during his cross-examination by ld.
Counsel for respondents which could assail his testimony or impeach its veracity.

19. It is well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs.
Himachal

Road Transport Corporation &
Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
20. Following observations in para 15 of aforesaid judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court being relevant are extracted herein below:
"15. In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied...."
21. Similar observation has been recorded by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007

22. FINDING:

Issue No.1 is therefore decided by holding that bodily injury suffered by Gaurav in motor vehicle accident on 08.12.2022 was caused as a result of rash and negligent driving of Taxi No.DL-1ZD-2211 by respondent Pawan Kumar (driver- cum-owner) which vehicle was insured with ACKO General Insurance Co.
23. Issue No.2 Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation if so, what amount and from whom?

Injured Gaurav having suffered linear undisplaced longitudinal fracture with multiple soft tissue injury was treated at Maharaja Aggarsen Hospital from 09.12.2022 to 10.12.2022 and continued to visit hospital as OPD Patient till 30.05.2023.
Quantum of compensation is required to be assessed separately under pecuniary and non-pecuniary heads.

25. At the outset, it has to be borne in mind that compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly and Courts & Tribunals have a duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the amount of compensation which should be just.
What would be "just" compensation is a vexed question.
There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb.
Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations.

It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Helen C. Rebello Vs.
Maharasthra SRTC, 1999 (1) SCC 90.
26.

sentences.text: "9. Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which are capable of being calculated in terms of money; whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non-pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e.
on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e., on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, hardship,

sentences.text:
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii),
(v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

19. It is well settled law that negligence of the driver in case of road traffic accident is required to be established on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs.
Del 1700 by holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence Gaurav vs Pawan Kumar on 2 December, 2025
strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
25. At the outset, it has to be borne in mind that compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly and Courts & Tribunals have a duty to weigh the various factors and quantify the amount of compensation which should be just.
What would be "just" compensation is a vexed question.
There can be no golden rule applicable to all cases for measuring the value of human life or a limb.
Measure of damages cannot be arrived at by precise mathematical calculations.
It would depend upon the particular facts and circumstances, and attending peculiar or special features, if any, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Helen C. Rebello Vs.
Maharasthra SRTC, 1999 (1) SCC 90.

shall, as respects such liabilities as are required to be covered by a policy under clause (b) of sub- section (1) of section 147, be of no effect."

Hence, omission of proviso to sub-section (4) of section 149 granting recovery right to the insurance company regarding so much of the policy as purports to restrict the insurance of the persons insured by reference to any conditions other than those in clause (b) of sub-section (2) will not exonerate insurance company from its statutory liability under section 150 sub- section (1) of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 to compensate victims even in case of violation of the terms & conditions of the policy w.r.t. permit, licence and/or driving under the influence of alcohol or drug as provided under section 150 sub-section (2) of the Act.
